headline: Doom runs on regular expressions, rendering a frame in 180 seconds with 14M substitutions
summary: A coder achieved the feat of running the classic 1992 game Doom using only regular expressions, a text-matching utility language. This unusual implementation requires 180 seconds to render a single frame, involving nearly 14 million substitutions.
details: A daring coder, Artem Lytkin, has successfully managed to get the classic 1992 game Doom running entirely on regular expressions. This extraordinary programming feat results in a single frame of game output taking around 180 seconds to produce.

Developers often consider regular expressions (regexes) a powerful but 'write-only' utility language for text finding and replacement. While complex, they fulfill the technical requirements to be considered a programming language, making this implementation possible.

Lytkin created a 96 MB plain-text string that functions as the virtual CPU's registers, RAM, video output (framebuffer), and the game's WAD data. The regex then performs text-matching and substitutions within this string to simulate processor operations and memory access.

Each frame requires nearly 14 million substitutions to render, with the engine firing 80,000 text substitutions per second. Lytkin describes the gameplay as "closer to correspondence chess with a shotgun than to a twitch shooter" due to the extreme slowness.

The memory access part was ingeniously implemented as a binary tree, using standard regex character-jump instructions to navigate branches. This avoids scanning the entire 96 MB text repeatedly, ensuring the game runs "before the heat death of the universe."

A demo of the doom-regex repository is available for download, and the project's website visually demonstrates the regex machine in action. Watching the substitutions occur is described as a mesmerizing experience.

headline_marked: [[Samsung’s chip workers are jumping ship]] to rival SK Hynix amid AI chip talent war
headline: Samsung’s chip workers are jumping ship to rival SK Hynix amid AI chip talent war
summary: The intensifying competition for AI chip dominance is fueling a fierce battle for skilled engineers, leading to significant talent shifts between industry giants.
details: The global race for AI chip supremacy is intensifying, leading to a critical shortage of specialized talent. This fierce competition is now causing significant employee movement between leading semiconductor firms.

Samsung, a major player in memory and logic chips, is reportedly seeing some of its skilled chip workers depart for its rival, SK Hynix. This talent migration highlights the high demand for expertise in advanced chip manufacturing.

SK Hynix has recently gained an edge in high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, crucial for AI accelerators, which may be attracting top talent. The company's focus on next-generation AI memory solutions makes it a desirable destination for experienced engineers.

This internal industry shift underscores the strategic importance of human capital in the semiconductor sector. Companies are investing heavily in recruitment and retention to secure their position in the rapidly evolving AI hardware landscape.
